questions.question: Describe the steps of the ruler method for measuring a straight-line distance on a map.
questions.expected_answer: Find the two places. Place the ruler's zero on the centre of the first dot and read the distance in centimetres at the centre of the second dot. Multiply the measurement by the word scale. For example, ten centimetres at one centimetre represents fifty kilometres is five hundred kilometres.

questions.question: Describe the steps of the paper strip method.
questions.expected_answer: Lay the edge of a paper strip so it touches the centres of both places. Make a pencil mark at each place and label them. Move the strip to the line scale and put the first mark on the zero. Read the distance where the second mark falls. If the distance is longer than the line scale, mark the end, slide the strip and add the pieces.

questions.question: Explain why the road distance between Johannesburg and Durban is longer than the straight-line distance.
questions.expected_answer: The straight-line distance goes directly from one place to the other, as the crow flies, about five hundred kilometres. Roads cannot go straight; they bend around mountains, follow valleys, cross rivers at bridges and pass through towns, so the road distance is about five hundred and seventy kilometres.
